summary: Read the typesafe-ai SKILL.md locally and summarized the three primitives (Choice/Score/Noul), the state-vs-instructions-vs-criteria design rules, and the compose-and-verify guidance. Then proposed seven concrete Jev questions (one speculative) to evaluate developer transcripts on prompting specificity, context completeness, model-choice appropriateness, skill-usage gaps, which-skill gap, verification discipline, and prompt iteration quality, with primitive type, draft instructions, criteria/options, and required state fields for each.
decisions: Chose Score for Q1 (prompting specificity) and Q2 (context completeness) because each is an ordered degree along a described dimension with concrete L1-L4 levels.

Chose Choice (not Score) for Q3 (model-choice appropriateness) because the result is one of a defined set of mutually-exclusive routing buckets (under-powered / appropriate / over-powered / cannot-tell).
Chose Noul for Q4 (skill usage gap present) and Q6 (verification discipline) because each is an independent yes/no condition with no confidence dimension.
Chose to make Q5 (which skill gap) a separate speculative Choice that runs in parallel with Q4, so that if Q4=no the speculative answer is ignored rather than blocking the call.
Decided to run Q1-Q7 in parallel over the same transcript state, and to issue a sequential follow-up only if Q4=yes (to fetch skill docs or pinpoint the omission).
Defined assumed state shape as { transcript.text, transcript.messages[], repo.context?, task.prompt? } plus repo.available_skills[] for the skill-gap questions and transcript.model for Q3.
